findings.issue: decodeURIComponent is applied to route params that Next 16 already decodes during route matching; a name that decodes to something containing '%' (e.g. /pokemon/a%25b) throws URIError and becomes a 500 instead of the spec'd Not found page. Same pattern in moves/[name]/page.tsx:13, abilities/[name]/page.tsx:12, types/[name]/page.tsx:24.
findings.suggestion: Delete the decodeURIComponent calls and pass params straight to getSpecies/getMove/getAbility/getType; the API's 404 already drives notFound().

findings.issue: The Moves section awaits every per-move fetch before the page paints, and the app has no error.tsx or loading.tsx, so API failures or the slow fan-out surface as the bare framework error page / blank wait.
findings.suggestion: Add a root error.tsx (and optionally a loading.tsx or Suspense boundary around the Moves section) for graceful degradation against the live API.

findings.issue: Filter/pagination query strings are hand-built in three places: pageHref (page.tsx:20), href (filters.tsx:11), and an inline template in game-select.tsx:29 — they can drift (e.g. page-param handling, encoding rules).
findings.suggestion: Extract one small shared query-string helper (e.g. lib/query.ts) used by both the server pagination links and the client filter navigation.

findings.issue: The species → default variety → Pokémon resolution logic is duplicated between loadMembers (team page) and loadSpecies (pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:41-47).
findings.suggestion: Move a getDefaultPokemon(species) helper into lib/api.ts and reuse it from both pages.

findings.issue: Inconsistent mutation pattern: RemoveButton refreshes the server page after writing the cookie (remove-button.tsx:15) while TeamButton only updates local state, relying on Next's zero-staleTime router cache to keep other pages fresh; cross-tab or future staleTime changes would desync the button from the rest of the app.
findings.suggestion: Pick one pattern — either router.refresh() after toggle in TeamButton too, or drop it from RemoveButton and lean fully on local state.

findings.issue: apiUrl constructs new URL(pathOrUrl) twice per absolute URL (pathname and search computed separately).
findings.suggestion: Parse once: const u = new URL(pathOrUrl); use u.pathname + u.search.

findings.issue: eslint-disable comments for @next/next/no-img-element but no ESLint config or dependency exists in the app, so the annotations are decorative and the lint rule they document is never enforced.
findings.suggestion: Either add eslint + eslint-config-next to devDependencies (with the rule active) or drop the stale comments and keep the plain prose justification.

findings.issue: turbopack.root: import.meta.dirname is a no-op here since app/ is the project root; it exists only for monorepo layouts where the root differs from cwd.
findings.suggestion: Remove it unless the app is expected to be built from outside its directory.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic, well-documented Next 16 app — React cache dedupe, connection()-driven dynamic rendering, clean server-only boundaries, bounded fetch caching, and spec-shaped naming make it fast to read and easy to own. The feature change followed the existing conventions faithfully. I'd merge after one light round: fix the double-decoded params (500 where 404 belongs), add error/loading boundaries for the API fan-out, and consolidate the three URL builders.
